subtitle: Measure first. Let AI assist.
description: A non-safety bench fixture for checking a disc with bought supports and a movable indicator arm. It gives inspection a repeatable physical datum while electronics and AI stay at requirements level.
targets: Proposed requirement, not a part acceptance limit
Ten-to-one study rule; full uncertainty needed
decisions: Buy calibrated indicators and supports; fabricate the base and adjustable brackets.
Separate model anomaly detection from final dimensional acceptance.
Tie each reading to part, fixture, instrument, calibration and environmental records.
materials: Base: machined steel candidate; stiffness and stability require assessment.
Arms: aluminium 6082-T6 candidate; non-load-bearing metrology supports.
Indicators and centres: purchased calibrated equipment.
risks: No measurement-system analysis or uncertainty budget has been completed.
Fixture and datum errors can dominate small runout readings.
steps: Level and qualify the base and purchased centres.
Mount the rotor without distorting its datum surfaces.
Set a calibrated probe normal to the inspected face.
Record repeated rotations, remounts and operator variation before acceptance use.
validation: Comparison with calibrated reference artefacts and independent CMM measurement.
hypotheses: Timed digital versus manual inspection report creation.
Demonstrate uncertainty and false-alarm rates before use.
sensors: Define displacement range/resolution, triggering, sampling, DAQ, traceable calibration, environmental sensing, storage and human approval workflow.
